newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields close higher despite dollar rebound.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields close higher despite dollar rebound.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.40 PCT (PREV 9.50) US 30-YR 6.40 (PREV 6.43)
* Yields end higher even though currency recovers
* Market thin and trendless
* Birch comments on fiscal position little impact
New Zealand yields ended mostly higher on Thursday despite a rebound in the New Zealand dollar to the eight-and-a-half year highs seen on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market was relatively thin and trendless, particularly in the bonds.

The 90-day bank bills opened up about four points weaker when the Trade-Weighted Index opened up abour 40 basis points lower but the recovery in the index later in the session was not matched in the bills.
The bid tone returned but there was little price action.
One dealer predicted the short-end would rally with quite a rush, possibly around the futures closeout on December 11.
"At the moment people don't want to take yields too much lower because the cost of carrying assets is so high," he said.
There was mild interest in morning comments from caretaker Finance Minister Bill Birch predicting that interest rates would fall as the inflation rate fell back into the 0-2 percent range next year.
Bankers Trust economist David Plank said Birch's comments that inflation numbers would be slightly lower than previously predicted "had few immediate implications".
